name: AI Services
purpose: This exam assesses your understanding of major AI services, your ability to choose suitable services for different situations, and responsible use.

domains.name: AI services and features from the three major providers

guide:
### 1. Introduction

**Purpose**: This exam assesses whether candidates understand the roles of major AI services and features, can select services for workplace objectives, and can use them responsibly.

**Objectives**

- Distinguish companies, models, products, features, and plans across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google
- Select services and features for conversation, search, research, projects, content creation, and external app connections
- Explain the purposes of coding tools and APIs and distinguish them from end-user services
- Apply principles of output verification, privacy, fairness, transparency, and human oversight
- Explain the purposes and differences of major third-party AI services

### 2. Target candidates

- Marketing and content specialists, researchers, service planners, AI training specialists

**Recommended background and exam scope**

- No prior certification, coding experience, or paid subscription is required.
- Writing code, training models, and designing architectures are outside the scope. Memorization of prices, usage limits, and model rankings is not assessed.

### 3. Content domains

| Domain | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| 1. AI services and features from the three major providers | 70% |
| 2. AI ethics and responsible use | 20% |
| 3. The wider AI services ecosystem | 10% |

**Domain 1: AI services and features from the three major providers**

- Knowledge: Differences among companies, models, products, features, and plans; ordinary conversation versus web search and research; projects and personalization; document, data, and image tasks; external app connections; purposes of coding tools and APIs
- Skills: Select features for workplace objectives and usage environments, explain differences between similar features, and distinguish external app read permissions, action permissions, and approval requirements
- Service scope: OpenAI ChatGPT app connections, agents, and Codex; Anthropic Claude Projects, Research, Artifacts, and Claude Code; Google Gemini Gems, Live, Deep Research, Workspace integration, AI Studio, APIs, and Gemini Notebook
- The full exam includes 12 questions each for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, plus six cross-provider comparison questions.

**Domain 2: AI ethics and responsible use**

- Knowledge: Hallucinations and uncertainty, privacy and confidentiality, bias and fairness, disclosure of AI use and sources, human oversight, misuse prevention, and user responsibility
- Skills: Identify when outputs need verification, decide whether sensitive information may be entered, place human review before important judgments, and select appropriate protection and disclosure measures in real usage situations
- Reference framework: Distinguish the roles of the providers' technical and research explanations, behavioral principles and safety frameworks, and product help and usage policies. Memorization of internal figures or safety thresholds is not assessed.

**Domain 3: The wider AI services ecosystem**

- Knowledge: Source-based search and research, academic discovery and writing, open-model, dataset, and demo platforms, image, video, and audio generation, and AI embedded in workplace tools
- Skills: Select services for a purpose, verify search sources, consult model cards for limitations and biases, and determine usage conditions and disclosure needs for generated content
- Service scope: Core purposes and differences of major third-party services such as Perplexity, Liner, Hugging Face, and Adobe Firefly. Model development and training are outside the scope.

questions.title: Search for questions that need current information
questions.prompt: An employee on Hanbit Trading’s planning team wants to use ChatGPT to find changes to industry regulations announced this month, with links to the sources. Which feature is **most appropriate**?

options.text: Enter the question in sidebar search to find the regulatory changes.
Use web search to find current information and check the source links in the answer.
Create a Project and organize the regulation names as chat titles.
Ask Memory to store the regulatory changes.

questions.explanation:
ChatGPT web search finds current information and displays relevant source links. It can search automatically when a question needs current information, or you can select it from the tools menu. Responses may include citations that you can select to open the sources. Search results can still be incomplete, outdated, or incorrect, so check the sources when accuracy matters.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Sidebar search is separate from web search and searches only your chats, projects, and files. It cannot find newly announced regulations.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Web search provides current information and source links.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Projects group related chats, files, and instructions; they do not retrieve new information.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Memory remembers information you provide for personalization. It cannot retrieve new regulations it does not yet know.

**Sources**: [ChatGPT search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Characteristics of deep research
questions.prompt: A planner at Nuri Logistics wants to use ChatGPT deep research to create a market research report drawing on multiple sources. Select **2 correct statements** about deep research.

options.text: It cannot use uploaded files and researches only publicly available web sources.
Before research begins, it may ask clarifying questions and present a research plan that you can review and edit.
Reports provide only brief conclusions without source references.
When using supported connected apps as sources, it uses read-only actions.
Its scope is fixed to the entire web and cannot be restricted to specific websites.

questions.explanation:
Deep research plans and investigates complex questions, then synthesizes its findings into a structured report. It may ask clarifying questions before starting and present a research plan for you to review and edit. Available connected apps, such as Google Drive and SharePoint, can serve as sources. It uses only read actions in those apps, and connecting an app does not change permissions at the provider.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: By default, it uses both the public web and uploaded files, and it can also use specified websites or connected apps.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Clarifying questions and an editable research plan are part of the deep research workflow.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Every report includes citations or source links, and the report view includes a section listing the sources used.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: The documentation states that only read actions are used with connected apps.
- **{{option:E}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Site management settings let you restrict research to specific domains or prioritize those sites while allowing broader web searches.

Additional note: Reading and analyzing many sources takes longer than regular search. Search or ordinary chat is recommended for urgent questions.

**Sources**: [Deep research in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10500283-deep-research) · [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt)

questions.title: Projects for ongoing work
questions.prompt: An employee on Hanbit Trading’s marketing team is preparing a product launch over several weeks. They want to keep related chats, reference files, and working instructions together and return to them later. Which **ChatGPT feature is most appropriate**?

options.text: Projects
Writing blocks
Voice mode
Data analysis

questions.explanation:
Projects bring related chats, files, and instructions together so that ChatGPT can use that context. They support ongoing activities such as writing, research, and planning, can be reused for recurring work, and let you continue across devices.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: This feature groups chats, files, and instructions together.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Writing blocks are editable areas for draft text within a conversation, not a way to organize multiple chats and files.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Voice mode enables spoken conversation; it does not store work context.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Data analysis analyzes uploaded data and creates tables and charts.

**Sources**: [Using Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt) · [ChatGPT capabilities overview](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9260256-chatgpt-capabilities-overview)

questions.title: Instructions that apply only within a Project
questions.prompt: A Nuri Logistics employee has entered “Keep answers short” in ChatGPT’s global settings. In a new quarterly report Project, however, they want detailed explanations for each item. What is the **most appropriate approach** without affecting other chats?

options.text: Change the global Custom instructions to “Give detailed answers.”
Upload a document containing the instructions as a Project file and leave the instructions field empty.
Enter a request for detailed explanations in Instructions in the Project settings.
Write the preferred response style in a writing block.

questions.explanation:
Instructions in Project settings apply only within that Project and take precedence over global Custom instructions. Adding a request for detailed responses to the report Project therefore preserves the short-answer setting for other chats.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: missing a condition)**: Changing the global setting also affects all chats outside the Project.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Project files serve as reference material; a separate instructions feature controls response behavior.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Project instructions apply only to that Project and override global settings.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Writing blocks are areas for editing draft text within a chat, not settings for saving response preferences.

**Sources**: [Using Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Custom instructions versus Memory
questions.prompt: A Hanbit Trading employee says, “I want to write down what ChatGPT should know about me and how I want it to respond.” Which feature lets the user write these instructions directly, rather than having ChatGPT use information accumulated through conversations?

options.text: Saved memories
Reference chat history
Project files
Custom instructions

questions.explanation:
Custom instructions let users write information that ChatGPT should consider when responding. On the web and desktop, they are configured under Personalization in Settings. Memory, in contrast, uses relevant information accumulated across conversations and other sources.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Saved memories are information you asked ChatGPT to remember or that it judged useful enough to save.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Reference chat history uses relevant past conversations, and what is used varies according to ChatGPT’s judgment.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Project files are reference material for a Project, not a global response setting.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: Guidance written directly by the user belongs in Custom instructions.

**Sources**: [ChatGPT Custom Instructions](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8096356-chatgpt-custom-instructions) · [Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Chatting without adding to Memory
questions.prompt: A Nuri Logistics employee wants to discuss a personnel-related concern with ChatGPT without having the conversation reflected in Memory. What is the **most appropriate approach**?

options.text: Start chatting, then change whether Memory is used during the conversation.
Start a Temporary chat.
Turn off only Reference chat history and chat as usual.
Proceed on the assumption that deleting saved memories afterward also removes mentions from past chats.

questions.explanation:
Temporary chat does not create or update memories. Before starting, you can choose whether to use Memory, Custom instructions, and plugins. These choices cannot be changed after the conversation begins.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: missing a condition)**: These Temporary chat choices must be made before starting and cannot be changed once the conversation begins.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Temporary chat does not create or update memories.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Turning off Reference chat history does not affect saved memories, so it does not guarantee that no new memories will be saved.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Deleting a saved memory prevents its use for future personalization, but mentions in past conversations remain.

**Sources**: [Memory FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-faq)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Editing a draft directly in a conversation
questions.prompt: A Hanbit Trading employee wants to select and edit a press release draft directly within a ChatGPT conversation and ask ChatGPT to rewrite some paragraphs. Which feature displays draft text, such as emails and documents, in an editable area?

options.text: Voice mode
Data analysis
Writing blocks
Search

questions.explanation:
OpenAI’s help documentation describes writing blocks as editable areas for draft text such as emails, messages, social posts, and documents. You can edit the text directly or ask ChatGPT to rewrite a selected passage or the entire draft. Code is handled similarly in code blocks.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Voice mode enables spoken conversation.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Data analysis analyzes and visualizes uploaded data.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Writing blocks provide an editable area for directly changing draft text or requesting revisions within a conversation.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Web search finds current information and answers with sources.

Additional note: The May 28, 2026 release notes state that canvas is no longer available with GPT-5.5 Instant and GPT-5.5 Thinking; writing and coding are supported within conversations through writing blocks and code blocks. Paid users can continue using canvas with legacy models for a limited time.

**Sources**: [Working with writing blocks and code blocks in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001246-working-with-writing-blocks-and-code-blocks-in-chatgpt) · [Model Release Notes](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Characteristics of data analysis
questions.prompt: An operations employee at Nuri Logistics uploads monthly delivery records in Excel to ChatGPT to examine trends. Select **2 correct statements** about data analysis.

options.text: It can analyze an uploaded spreadsheet and produce tables or charts.
It calls external APIs from its code execution environment to retrieve the latest delivery data directly.
Some tasks are analyzed by running Python code, so it is advisable to review the code, outputs, and assumptions before using the results.
It always extracts tables from scanned images accurately.
All charts are static images and cannot be interactive.

questions.explanation:
Data analysis answers questions about uploaded files, creates tables and charts, summarizes rows, columns, trends, and outliers, and explains assumptions and next steps. For some tasks, it writes and runs Python. The help documentation recommends reviewing the generated code, outputs, and assumptions before relying on the results.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Analyzing uploaded files and presenting tables or charts is a core capability.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: The Python environment cannot make external web requests or API calls, so data must be uploaded or connected.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: The documentation describes Python execution and recommends checking the results.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Image-based or scanned tables may not be extracted reliably.
- **{{option:E}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Bar, line, pie, and scatter charts can be converted into interactive charts.

**Sources**: [Data analysis with ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8437071-data-analysis-with-chatgpt) · [ChatGPT capabilities overview](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9260256-chatgpt-capabilities-overview)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Image input and image generation
questions.prompt: A designer at Hanbit Trading photographs a diagram drawn on a meeting-room whiteboard and uploads it to ChatGPT. They want an explanation of the diagram, followed by a newly created introductory illustration on the same topic. Which capabilities handle these two requests?

options.text: Voice mode and Scheduled tasks
Writing blocks and Data analysis
Deep research and Projects
Image input (analysis) and image generation

questions.explanation:
ChatGPT can analyze uploaded images, diagrams, and charts, generate images from text prompts, and edit generated images. Explaining the photographed diagram uses image input; creating a new illustration uses image generation.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Voice mode enables spoken conversation, while Scheduled tasks performs one-time or recurring tasks. Neither corresponds to these image requests.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Writing blocks edit draft text, and Data analysis analyzes data files.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Deep research performs multistep research, while Projects groups chats and files.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: Image analysis and image generation respectively correspond to the two requests.

**Sources**: [ChatGPT capabilities overview](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9260256-chatgpt-capabilities-overview)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Three things apps can do
questions.prompt: ChatGPT Apps (connected services) can **read/search, display, and act** in connected services. Which example represents **Act**?

options.text: Create a new task or update an existing task in a connected work management service.
Find a document in connected file storage and consult its contents.
Display an interface such as a map or card within the conversation.
Index content from a connected service in advance to make responses faster.

questions.explanation:
OpenAI’s help documentation divides app capabilities into three categories. Read/search finds and consults information in connected services. Display shows interfaces such as maps, cards, and documents within a conversation. Act performs supported actions, such as creating or updating information in a service.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Creating or updating information within a service is an action.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Finding and consulting information is read/search.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Showing an interface in the conversation is display.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Some apps synchronize and index content in advance. This describes an access method (sync), rather than one of the three capability categories.

**Sources**: [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: The relationship between plugins and apps
questions.prompt: An IT employee at Hanbit Trading is introducing ChatGPT plugins to colleagues. Which statement about the relationship between plugins and apps is **correct**?

options.text: Installing a plugin skips app authentication and workspace permissions.
Every plugin must include an app that connects to an external service.
Plugin and app are two names for exactly the same thing.
A plugin packages capabilities into a workflow and can contain apps, skills, or both.

questions.explanation:
OpenAI’s help documentation describes a plugin as capabilities packaged into a workflow, which can contain apps, skills, or both. Some plugins contain only skills and do not connect to external services. Installing a plugin does not bypass app authentication or workspace permissions.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Installing a plugin cannot bypass app authentication or workspace permissions.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Some plugins contain only skills and do not connect to external services.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Apps connect external services to ChatGPT; plugins package apps or skills together.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: This matches the definition in the help documentation.

**Sources**: [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Choosing an app permission option
questions.prompt: A security employee at Nuri Logistics wants ChatGPT to ask the user first in every case, whether reading information from a connected service or performing an action. Which app permission option is appropriate?

options.text: Allow read actions
Allow low-risk actions
Always ask
Allow all actions

questions.explanation:
App permission options determine when ChatGPT asks the user for confirmation. Always ask requires confirmation before reading information or performing any action.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: missing a condition)**: Allow read actions skips confirmation for read actions.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: missing a condition)**: Allow low-risk actions is the default when no other setting applies. Sensitive actions can still require approval or be denied. It does not ask in every case.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: It asks before reads and all other actions.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: missing a condition)**: Allow all actions is available only for eligible apps or accounts and carries greater risk because actions may run without additional confirmation.

**Sources**: [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt) · [Managing app permissions in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001495-managing-app-permissions-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: What app permission settings mean
questions.prompt: Hanbit Trading’s information security team is explaining ChatGPT app permission settings in staff training. Select **2 correct statements**.

options.text: Selecting Allow read actions gives the app new write access.
Selecting Always ask disconnects the app.
App permissions determine when ChatGPT requests confirmation; they do not give an app new access.
Even if an administrator disables an app and “Disabled by admin” appears, users can use it by changing their permission option.
An app’s access is determined by the app itself, access granted when connecting, and workspace controls.

questions.explanation:
OpenAI’s help documentation explains that app permissions control only when ChatGPT asks; they do not grant new access. App access comes from the app itself, access granted at connection, and workspace controls. To remove access, disconnect the app or have the workspace administrator disable it.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: This option only skips confirmation for reads; it does not grant new write access.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Always ask controls confirmation behavior and does not disconnect the app.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: This is the documentation’s central explanation.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: “Disabled by admin” means an administrator must change the setting; a user cannot resolve it.
- **{{option:E}} (Correct)**: This matches the documentation’s explanation of where access comes from.

**Sources**: [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt) · [Managing app permissions in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001495-managing-app-permissions-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Working with computer files unavailable on the web
questions.prompt: A Nuri Logistics employee starts Work in ChatGPT in a web browser and asks it to organize files in a work folder on their laptop into a report, but it cannot access those files. What is the **appropriate response**?

options.text: Use Work in the desktop app and explicitly allow access to computer files.
Use Codex CLI, a software development tool, to create the same report.
Make the same request in the mobile app to access the computer files.
Approve file access by voice and send the request again.

questions.explanation:
Work is an agent that handles longer, multistep tasks and creates deliverables such as documents, spreadsheets, and reports. According to the help documentation, Work on the web and mobile cannot access files on the user’s computer, while the desktop app can do so with permission. Actions requiring approval on the web and mobile are approved through on-screen controls; voice approval is not supported.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Computer file access is available in the desktop app when permission is granted.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect: confusing similar features)**: Codex is for software development and technical tasks such as writing, debugging, and testing code, rather than general document-organization reports.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Work on mobile also cannot access computer files.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Voice approval is not supported; approval uses on-screen controls.

**Sources**: [ChatGPT Work and Codex](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Steps for connecting and using an app
questions.prompt:
A Hanbit Trading employee is using a connected service in ChatGPT for the first time. Arrange these four steps in the **correct order**, following the documented workflow.

- ({{option:가}}) Review any approval request before ChatGPT reads information or performs an action.
- ({{option:나}}) Select the app and complete sign-in or authorization.
- ({{option:다}}) Use the app in a conversation by mentioning it with @ or selecting it from the + menu.
- ({{option:라}}) Open Apps or Plugins.

items.text: Review any approval request before ChatGPT reads information or performs an action.
Select the app and complete sign-in or authorization.
Use the app in a conversation by mentioning it with @ or selecting it from the + menu.
Open Apps or Plugins.

questions.explanation:
The documentation instructs users to open Apps or Plugins, select an app and complete sign-in or authorization, then use the app through an @ mention or the + menu. During use, ChatGPT may request approval before reading information or performing an action.

| Order | Step | Dependency on the preceding step | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | ({{option:라}}) Open Apps or Plugins | None. First open the screen where you can choose an app. | Starting point for connection |
| 2 | ({{option:나}}) Select the app and complete sign-in and authorization | Select the app in ({{option:라}}) before proceeding. | The connection must be completed before the app can access the service. |
| 3 | ({{option:다}}) Use the app with @ or the + menu | The connection in ({{option:나}}) must be completed before use in a conversation. | How to invoke an app |
| 4 | ({{option:가}}) Review approval requests | Requests appear before reads or actions while using the app in ({{option:다}}). | Approval requests occur during use. |

**Sources**: [Connectors in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775-connectors-in-chatgpt)
tags: AI services and features from the three major providers

questions.title: Matching needs to features
questions.prompt: Match Hanbit Trading employees’ needs to ChatGPT features. Choose the most appropriate feature on the right for each need on the left. One item on the right is not used.

options.text: Codex
Work
Writing blocks
Projects
Search
Voice mode

items.text: Create finished deliverables such as reports or presentations through research and analysis
Review code in a repository and run tests
Check today’s news with source links
Edit a draft directly within a conversation or ask for it to be rewritten
Keep chats, files, and instructions for work spanning several weeks together

questions.explanation:
Distinguish each feature by the work it is designed for. Work creates deliverables, Codex handles code, Search finds current information, writing blocks edit drafts, and Projects organizes context.

| Item | Decisive reason |
| --- | --- |
| 1 → {{option:b}} | Work is an agent that handles longer, multistep tasks and creates deliverables such as documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and reports. |
| 2 → {{option:a}} | Codex is a software development tool that writes and debugs code, runs tests and commands, and reviews changes. |
| 3 → {{option:e}} | Web search finds current information and displays source links. |
| 4 → {{option:c}} | Writing blocks are editable areas for directly changing draft text or requesting revisions within a conversation. |
| 5 → {{option:d}} | Projects groups related chats, files, and instructions. |
| {{option:f}} | Voice mode enables spoken conversation. None of these needs requires it, so it is not used. |

**Sources**: [ChatGPT Work and Codex](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001275-chatgpt-work-and-codex) · [ChatGPT search](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search) · [Working with writing blocks and code blocks in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001246-working-with-writing-blocks-and-code-blocks-in-chatgpt) · [Using Projects in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-using-projects-in-chatgpt)

questions.title: Where uploaded Project knowledge is used
questions.prompt: Hanbit Trading’s marketing team uploads a product brochure and glossary to the knowledge section of a Claude Project. How are these materials used?

options.text: They are referenced only in the one conversation where they were uploaded.
They serve as reference context in all conversations within the same Project.
They are automatically referenced in every conversation outside the Project as well.
Claude reads only the Project name and description, and looks at file contents only when separately asked.

questions.explanation:
Projects are workspaces that collect related materials and instructions. Claude’s help documentation states that files, text, and code snippets uploaded to Project knowledge provide context for all conversations within that Project. This removes the need to paste the same material into each conversation.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect: scope too narrow)**: This describes a file attached to a single conversation. Project knowledge is used across conversations in the Project.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Project knowledge serves as context for all conversations in that Project.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect: scope too broad)**: Project knowledge is used within its Project and does not extend to conversations outside it.

- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect: factual error)**: Connector access is limited to the scope the user can already access in that service.
- **{{option:E}} (Correct)**: Connectors retrieve data and perform actions within the user's existing access scope.

questions.title: Comparing Projects in ChatGPT and Claude
questions.prompt: Hanbit Trading's marketing manager says, "I do not want to paste the same campaign materials and instructions every time," and compares Projects in ChatGPT and Claude. Select **two** descriptions that match the official help documentation.

Claude projects are folders containing knowledge files but no chat history.

Both services allow reference materials to be added to a project and used in its conversations.
In ChatGPT, global custom instructions take precedence over project instructions.

questions.title: Handling a confidently worded AI answer
questions.prompt: A planning team employee at Saebom Trading asks AI about trends in a business partner’s industry. The AI replies with a detailed explanation and says, "I am certain." What is the most appropriate approach before including this answer in a report?

options.text: Include it as accurate information because the explanation is specific and confidently worded.
Include it unchanged because a longer, more detailed answer must have sufficient evidence.
Check reliable sources because it may be wrong regardless of its tone.
Skip further verification because the AI explicitly said it was certain.

questions.explanation:
Generative AI can express incorrect information confidently. OpenAI’s help article explains that ChatGPT can sound confident even when it is wrong and states that "Confidence isn’t reliability." It recommends checking important information against reliable sources. The OpenAI Model Spec also says models should express uncertainty when questions exceed their knowledge and be more cautious when incorrect information could have a greater impact. Confidence of tone is not evidence of accuracy, so a person must verify material used in a report.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Specific, definite wording does not guarantee accuracy. Fabricated information can use the same tone.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Length and detail do not demonstrate that evidence exists. A long, detailed answer can still be wrong.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Important information must be checked against sources regardless of the tone.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: An AI saying it is certain does not complete verification. That claim can accompany incorrect information.

**Sources**: [Does ChatGPT tell the truth? (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8313428-does-chatgpt-tell-the-truth) · [OpenAI Model Spec › Express uncertainty](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md)

questions.title: Information to avoid in conversations that human reviewers may see
questions.prompt: Google’s Gemini Apps guidance states that human reviewers may see some conversations and recommends not entering confidential information users would not want reviewers to see. An employee at Hanbit Trading checks this guidance before entering information. Which content should the employee **avoid entering**?

options.text: Company introduction text already published on its website.
Customer consultation records and contract terms that must not be disclosed externally.
Sentences from the company’s publicly released press statement.
An event schedule posted for anyone to view.

questions.explanation:
The Gemini Apps Privacy Hub advises users not to enter confidential information they would not want human reviewers to see because some conversations may be reviewed. The pre-entry question is therefore whether it is acceptable for another person to see the content. Google’s AI Principles also treat privacy and security as an element of responsible development. Customer consultation records and contract terms are nonpublic information whose disclosure could cause harm, so they should be avoided.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Already public introduction text does not reveal new information when someone sees it.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Nonpublic customer information and contract terms are confidential information that reviewers should not see.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: A public press release is not confidential and can be entered for editing.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Information anyone can access does not create a disclosure risk.

Additional note: Services differ in how they retain, review, and use conversations for training. Check both the settings of the tool used for work and company guidelines.

**Sources**: [Gemini Apps Privacy Hub (Gemini Apps Help)](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961) · [Google AI Principles](https://ai.google/principles/)

questions.title: Evaluating identical submissions with different names
questions.prompt: An HR team uses AI to grade assignments from new employee training. Two submissions have exactly the same content and differ only in the author’s name. What result should be **expected** from a fair AI evaluation?

options.text: Infer gender from the names and slightly raise one score to balance the results.
Award a higher score to the submission with the more familiar name.
Accept different scores for identical content as unproblematic.
Apply the same criteria and award the same score regardless of irrelevant information such as names.

questions.explanation:
The OpenAI Model Spec’s "Uphold fairness" section says relevant context should be considered and irrelevant details ignored. When evaluating people or helping with decisions, models should not discriminate or show preferences based on demographic information or protected characteristics unless legally or contextually required. Similar situations should receive consistent reasoning and criteria. The Model Spec illustrates this with grading the same proof under different names. Anthropic’s Claude constitution also values equal and fair treatment of all individuals.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Inferring gender from a name and adjusting a score changes the evaluation based on irrelevant information.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Preferring a familiar name is a preference based on an irrelevant detail.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: The same criteria applied to identical content should yield the same result. A difference needs investigation.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: Ignoring irrelevant information and applying consistent criteria is fundamental to fairness.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Uphold fairness](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md) · [Claude's constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution) · [Google AI Principles](https://ai.google/principles/)

questions.title: When a customer asks whether a support chatbot is human
questions.prompt: Nuri Logistics names its customer support chatbot "Haru." During a conversation, a customer sincerely asks, "Am I speaking with a person right now?" Which response is most responsible?

options.text: Keep the name "Haru" but truthfully explain that the customer is speaking with AI.
Say it is a human support representative to build trust.
Avoid the question and redirect the conversation to the customer’s inquiry.
Give only the representative’s name and department without saying whether it is AI.

questions.explanation:
Anthropic’s Claude constitution says AI should not deny being AI when a user sincerely wants to know whether they are speaking with a human or AI. An operator may use a persona with a name and personality, but may not use it to deceive users in harmful ways. Anthropic’s Usage Policy also prohibits misleading users with bots that claim to be human. The appropriate response is to retain the name while disclosing that it is AI.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: The persona name can remain, but a sincere question should receive a truthful disclosure that it is AI.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Claiming to be human deceives the user and conflicts with the principle against denying AI identity.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Avoiding a sincere question can also leave the user believing they are speaking with a human.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Providing only a name and department creates the impression of a human representative and does not answer the question.

**Sources**: [Claude's constitution › Handling conflicts between operators and users](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution) · [Anthropic Usage Policy › Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup)

questions.title: Why an AI agent asks for confirmation before acting
questions.prompt: A Saebom Trading employee asks an AI agent to handle a payment request for a business partner. Just before submitting the form, the agent asks, "Shall I proceed?" What is the **main reason** for this confirmation step?

options.text: To deliberately slow responses and reduce service usage.
Because the model does not know how to do the task and is handing it to a person instead.
To reduce unintended consequences by having a person confirm actions with substantial, hard-to-reverse effects.
Because it is a legal requirement only for personal-account users.

questions.explanation:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT agent help article describes user confirmation for consequential actions as a safeguard and explains that the agent pauses to ask when needed. (As of the reference date, that product has been discontinued and users are directed to ChatGPT Work, but the same design principle appears in the Model Spec.) The OpenAI Model Spec says an agent’s autonomy must have an agreed scope, irreversible side effects should be minimized, and the agent should pause when approval is needed. Actions such as payments and sending messages are difficult to reverse, so final human confirmation is a responsible design.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Confirmation manages risk; it is not intended to control speed or reduce usage.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: It checks human intent for consequential actions rather than compensating for not knowing how to act.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Human confirmation reduces unintended outcomes from consequential, hard-to-reverse actions.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: This is a product safeguard, not a legal obligation restricted to a particular account type.

**Sources**: [ChatGPT agent (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent) · [OpenAI Model Spec › Act within an agreed-upon scope of autonomy, Control and communicate side effects](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md)

questions.title: Requests for political persuasion targeting a specific group
questions.prompt: An employee on Hanbit Trading’s communications team asks AI to write several political texts. Which request does the OpenAI Model Spec say the AI **should not assist with**?

options.text: Rewrite an explanation of the electoral system in plain language for a local community information session.
Write an anti-candidate message designed to exploit the anxieties of women voters in their twenties.
Create a neutral table comparing policy pledges from different parties.
Explain types of rhetorical techniques used in political speeches, with examples.

questions.explanation:
The OpenAI Model Spec’s "Don’t facilitate the targeted manipulation of political views" section says not to provide advice, instructions, or content designed to manipulate the political views of particular individuals or demographic groups. Its examples include fear-based messages targeting groups of a particular age, race, or nationality. Political content for unspecified or broad audiences is allowed when it does not exploit a particular group’s vulnerabilities. The issue is the design to manipulate a targeted group, not the political topic itself.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: An explanation of the system provides information to a broad audience.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: This message exploits a specific group’s anxieties to change its views and should not be supported.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: A neutral comparison organizes information rather than manipulating people.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Explaining rhetorical techniques is general educational content.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Don't facilitate the targeted manipulation of political views](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md)

questions.title: Making citations in an AI-generated legal draft reliable
questions.prompt: Nuri Logistics’ legal team plans to share an AI-generated draft opinion at an internal meeting. The draft includes several case-law and academic-paper citations. Select **TWO** ways to improve the reliability of the citations.

options.text: Ask the AI once whether the citations are accurate and finish verification if it says yes.
Instruct it to use only the supplied materials and allow it to say it does not know when it cannot find evidence.
Locate the cited judgments and papers directly and check that the sources and content actually match.
Assume a publication exists if the citation is correctly formatted.
Ask the same question again and skip checking the originals if the wording is similar.

questions.explanation:
AI can invent plausible quotations, studies, and sources that do not exist. Anthropic’s documentation recommends allowing the model to say it does not know, restricting it to provided documents, and requiring citations for claims. It also stresses that these techniques reduce rather than eliminate hallucinations, so important information must still be verified. OpenAI’s help article likewise recommends always checking quotations, data, and references to external documents.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Asking the same model again is not independent verification. It may confirm an invented citation.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Restricting the source material and allowing uncertainty reduces fabricated citations.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Direct comparison with the original source is the most reliable verification.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Correct formatting is not evidence that a publication exists. Fake citations can look plausible.
- **{{option:E}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Repeated similar wording does not show agreement with the original and cannot replace verification.

**Sources**: [Reduce hallucinations (Claude API Docs)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations) · [Does ChatGPT tell the truth? (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8313428-does-chatgpt-tell-the-truth)

questions.title: Asking an AI without search about recent changes
questions.prompt: An employee in Hanbit Trading’s administration team asks an AI chat tool without web search about changes to a labor-related notice revised this year. The AI lists specific changes. What should the employee do before using the answer in an internal announcement?

options.text: Publish it unchanged, treating the detailed list as evidence that it is current.
Use it because the model is described as the latest version, assuming it includes the revisions.
Repeat the question two or three times and finalize the answer if the responses are similar.
Check the official notice directly because the changes may postdate the model’s knowledge.

questions.explanation:
The OpenAI Model Spec identifies outdated information caused by training dates or a knowledge cutoff, and rapidly changing circumstances, as reasons for uncertainty. Without search, a model may produce a plausible answer without knowing recent revisions. OpenAI’s help article explains that search can retrieve current web information with sources and recommends opening source links when accuracy matters. Information whose currency is important, such as laws and official notices, should be checked against official documents.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Specific details are not evidence that the information is current.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Being the latest model does not necessarily mean it knows this year’s revisions; events after training may be unknown.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Repeated answers from the same model do not verify currency and may repeat the same error.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: Check recent information the model may not know directly against original sources such as official notices.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Express uncertainty](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md) · [Does ChatGPT tell the truth? (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8313428-does-chatgpt-tell-the-truth)

questions.title: Responding when AI refuses a request for private contact details
questions.prompt: A Nuri Logistics salesperson asks AI to find a business partner’s purchasing manager’s personal mobile number. The AI refuses, saying it cannot provide private contact details. What is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Contact the business through its main number or official work channel and request a connection to the appropriate person if needed.
Rephrase the request as urgent and ask again.
Try the same request in a different AI service to see whether it succeeds.
Collect scattered social media posts, paste them into AI, and ask it to infer the number.

questions.explanation:
The OpenAI Model Spec’s "Protect people’s privacy" section says not to comply with requests for private or sensitive personal information, even if it is available somewhere online. It distinguishes a public official’s office number from a personal mobile number, refusing the latter and demonstrating redirection to official contact channels. Anthropic’s Usage Policy also prohibits collecting or accessing personal information without permission. For business purposes, use the work channels the person has made public.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Official work channels meet the business objective without invading privacy.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Urgency does not change the privacy judgment.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Bypassing the refusal with another tool still involves collection without consent.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Combining scattered information to discover private contact details is also unauthorized collection.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Protect people's privacy](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md) · [Anthropic Usage Policy › Do Not Compromise Privacy or Identity Rights](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup)

questions.title: Checks before analyzing customer support records with AI
questions.prompt: Saebom Trading plans to enter customer support records into a company-approved AI tool to analyze complaint categories. The records contain customer names, contact details, and addresses. Select **TWO** actions to take before entering them.

options.text: Retain only what the analysis needs and mask identifying information such as names, contact details, and addresses.
Do not worry beforehand because deleting the conversation later removes all copies, including those reviewed by people.
Enter real names and contact details unchanged because the tool is used internally.
Check activity retention and model-improvement settings alongside company guidelines and configure them for the task.
Skip the security review because a paid service makes any data safe.

questions.explanation:
Entered content is transmitted to the service, so identifying information should be limited to what is needed. Services also differ in conversation retention, training use, and review. For example, the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub explains that conversations reviewed by people are not removed when activity is deleted and may be retained for up to three years. OpenAI’s data controls let users choose whether conversations are used to improve models, and Anthropic provides guidance on model-improvement settings for consumer accounts. Both masking information and checking settings and guidelines are necessary.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: The safest approach is not to enter identifying information unnecessary for the analysis in the first place.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Google says reviewed conversations are not removed by deleting activity. Deletion cannot replace pre-entry checks.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Internal use alone does not justify unrestricted entry of customer identifiers.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: Retention and training use vary by tool and settings and must be checked.
- **{{option:E}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Paid services still require a review of data handling and settings; payment does not establish that all data is safe.

**Sources**: [Gemini Apps Privacy Hub (Gemini Apps Help)](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961) · [Data controls FAQ (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7730893-data-controls-faq) · [Is my data used for model training? (Claude Privacy Center)](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023580-is-my-data-used-for-model-training)

questions.title: Using AI to screen job applications
questions.prompt: Saebom Trading’s recruiting team plans to have AI score 200 applicants’ documents and automatically reject those with low scores. Which approach is most responsible?

options.text: Have people review only high-scoring applicants and automatically reject low-scoring ones.
Assume there is no bias because names are masked and decide solely from the scores.
Use AI to organize applications and have people make selection and rejection decisions.
Add "evaluate fairly" to the prompt and automatically process applicants by score.

questions.explanation:
Hiring substantially affects people’s opportunities. Anthropic’s Usage Policy requires meaningful review by qualified people with authority to change AI recommendations in high-risk areas such as employment. OpenAI’s usage policies prohibit automating high-stakes decisions in sensitive areas without human review, and Google’s policy prohibits automated decisions with major adverse effects on individual rights without human oversight. Anthropic’s discrimination research shows that careful prompt design can greatly reduce bias while still opposing automated decisions in high-risk cases. AI should assist, and humans should decide.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Automatically rejecting low-scoring applicants is an automated decision without human review.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Masking names does not establish that bias is eliminated, and the problem of automated decisions remains.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: AI organizes information while people review it against criteria and make decisions.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: A single instruction cannot replace bias checks and human review.

**Sources**: [Anthropic Usage Policy › High-risk Use Case Requirements](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup) · [OpenAI Usage policies](https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies/) · [Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy](https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy) · [Evaluating and Mitigating Discrimination in Language Model Decisions (Anthropic)](https://www.anthropic.com/research/evaluating-and-mitigating-discrimination-in-language-model-decisions)

questions.title: The order of steps for checking bias in an AI evaluation tool
questions.prompt:
Hanbit Trading’s training team plans to introduce a tool that uses AI to summarize and evaluate learner assignments. Arrange the four bias-checking steps in the **correct order** before putting it into operation.

- ({{option:가}}) Compare results for otherwise identical inputs that differ only in evaluation-irrelevant attributes such as name or gender.
- ({{option:나}}) Put the checked tool into operation with a final human review procedure.
- ({{option:다}}) Define the evaluation criteria and distinguish attributes that must not affect the evaluation.
- ({{option:라}}) If results differ, revise the instructions and criteria, then compare again to verify.

items.text: Compare results for otherwise identical inputs that differ only in evaluation-irrelevant attributes such as name or gender.
Put the checked tool into operation with a final human review procedure.
Define the evaluation criteria and distinguish attributes that must not affect the evaluation.
If results differ, revise the instructions and criteria, then compare again to verify.

questions.explanation:
A bias check first defines which factors should and should not affect evaluation, then compares results from inputs that differ only in those factors. The OpenAI Model Spec illustrates this with grading the same proof under different names and calls for consistent criteria in similar situations. Anthropic’s research shows that model decisions can exhibit both positive and negative discrimination patterns and that careful prompt design can substantially reduce them.

- **Step 1 ({{option:다}})**: First define evaluation criteria and irrelevant attributes. Without them, you cannot know what to vary in the comparison.
- **Step 2 ({{option:가}})**: Submit identical content varying only the specified attributes and compare the results. A comparison is needed to identify differences.
- **Step 3 ({{option:라}})**: If differences appear, revise the instructions and criteria and compare again. The comparison identifies what needs correction.
- **Step 4 ({{option:나}})**: After checks and revisions, put the tool into operation with final human review. Deploying before checking would allow biased results to be used.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Uphold fairness](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md) · [Evaluating and Mitigating Discrimination in Language Model Decisions (Anthropic)](https://www.anthropic.com/research/evaluating-and-mitigating-discrimination-in-language-model-decisions)

questions.title: Using an AI answer that includes a source link
questions.prompt: A Nuri Logistics employee sees a market-size figure in a Gemini Apps answer with a source link attached. What is the most appropriate action before citing the figure in a report?

options.text: Cite it unchanged because the link means it is accurate.
Open the link and verify that the document actually contains the figure before citing it.
Use only answers with links because all answers without them are wrong.
Without opening the link, ask the same question again to see whether the same figure appears.

questions.explanation:
Gemini Apps explains that it provides sources and related links where possible for further exploration, and that not every response includes links or sources. OpenAI’s help article also recommends visiting links directly to check sources when accuracy matters. A displayed source only indicates where to check; a person must verify that the document actually contains the figure before citing it.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: A displayed link does not establish that the answer matches the document; this still needs checking.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Opening the link and comparing the original is the proper use of source references.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Not every response includes a source. No link does not necessarily mean an answer is wrong, but separate verification is needed.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Repeating the question is not a comparison with the original.

**Sources**: [Gemini Apps Help › Sources and related links in responses](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14143489) · [Does ChatGPT tell the truth? (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8313428-does-chatgpt-tell-the-truth)

questions.title: Transparency when publishing AI-generated content
questions.prompt: Saebom Trading’s marketing team plans to publish AI-generated images and text on social media. Select **TWO** appropriate judgments about transparency.

options.text: If Gemini Apps finds no traces of Google AI, conclude the content was not AI-generated.
Do not deceptively present AI-generated content as entirely human-created.
Assume Gemini Apps can identify AI-generated images regardless of which company’s tool made them.
Because Gemini Apps verification recognizes Google AI content only, another AI may have created content even when no result is found.
Trust the result unconditionally because AI-generation traces must remain even after minor image edits.

questions.explanation:
Google’s policy prohibits deceptive claims that AI-generated content was entirely human-created. Gemini Apps uses SynthID watermarks to check whether images, video, or audio were made with Google AI, but recognizes only content from Google AI tools. If no watermark is found, another AI system may have created it, and extensive editing may make traces undetectable. Verification is an aid, so creators should first avoid misleading others about AI use.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Absence of a detected trace does not prove the content was not AI-generated; another AI may have made it.
- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Deceptively presenting AI content as entirely human-created is prohibited by the policy.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Gemini Apps recognizes content generated by Google AI tools only.
- **{{option:D}} (Correct)**: The detection scope is limited to Google AI, so another AI remains a possibility when no result is found.
- **{{option:E}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: The watermark generally withstands resizing and color adjustments, but guidance notes that extensive edits can prevent detection, so persistence is not guaranteed.

**Sources**: [Verify AI-generated images, videos, and audio (Gemini Apps Help)](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16722517) · [Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy › Misinformation, misrepresentation, or misleading activities](https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy)

questions.title: Setting permissions for an agent organizing an inbox
questions.prompt: Hanbit Trading’s finance team wants an AI agent to organize an inbox for business partner inquiries. The agent can read messages, draft replies, send them, and delete them. What permission scope should be set before starting?

options.text: Allow reading and drafting, but require human confirmation before sending or deleting.
Give it read, send, and delete permissions to complete everything at once, then inspect the results later.
Require human approval for every message before either reading it or drafting a reply.
Start without defining a scope and adjust permissions if a problem occurs.

questions.explanation:
The OpenAI Model Spec allows agent autonomy within an agreed scope, calls for minimizing required access, and says to define in advance when the agent must stop for approval. It also calls for minimizing hard-to-reverse side effects such as sending or deleting, while noting that confirmation at every step is impractical. Allowing lower-risk reading and drafting autonomously while requiring approval for consequential actions follows this principle. OpenAI’s ChatGPT agent help article likewise describes user confirmation for consequential actions. (That product is discontinued as of the reference date.)

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Delegate lower-risk actions while humans confirm consequential actions such as sending and deleting.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Excess permissions can make mistaken sending or deletion lead to irreversible outcomes.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, constraint violation)**: Approval at every step defeats the purpose of delegation; focus approval on consequential actions.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Define scope before starting. Waiting for a problem can allow an irreversible action to occur first.

**Sources**: [OpenAI Model Spec › Act within an agreed-upon scope of autonomy, Control and communicate side effects](https://github.com/openai/model_spec/blob/main/model_spec.md) · [ChatGPT agent (OpenAI Help Center)](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent)

questions.title: Matching risky requests with responsible responses
questions.prompt: For each request on the left, choose the most appropriate responsible response on the right. One option on the right will not be used.

options.text: Inform the people concerned and proceed only after confirming consent or a legal basis.
Do not make the request; stop because the intent to deceive is clear.
Use only reviews from real customers and limit AI to polishing the wording.
Have a qualified person meaningfully review the recommendation with authority to change it, and inform the customer of AI use.
Switch to a higher-tier model and submit the same request again.

items.text: Generate large numbers of purchase reviews with AI as if written by nonexistent customers and post them to an online store.
Notify a customer of an insurance claim outcome based on an AI recommendation on whether to pay.
Use AI to draft an email impersonating a business partner’s representative to request a payment-account change.
Use AI analysis to track individual employees’ activities without their knowledge.

questions.explanation:
Responsible use depends on whether a request is deceptive, concerns a consequential decision, or requires individual consent. Anthropic’s Usage Policy prohibits fake accounts or reviews that misrepresent their origin and prohibits impersonation. For high-risk areas such as insurance and employment, it requires meaningful review by qualified people and disclosure of AI use. Anthropic and Google policies prohibit tracking or surveillance without consent.

- **1 → {{option:c}}**: Reviews from fictional customers misrepresent the origin of accounts and reviews. Use real customers’ reviews and AI only for assistance.
- **2 → {{option:d}}**: Insurance is a high-risk area. Do not simply communicate the recommendation; have a qualified person review it with authority to change it and disclose AI use.
- **3 → {{option:b}}**: Impersonating a business partner to change payment details has clear fraudulent intent. Stop rather than make the request.
- **4 → {{option:a}}**: Tracking without consent is prohibited. Inform the people concerned and proceed only when consent or a legal basis is confirmed.
- **{{option:e}}**: None of these situations is a model-performance problem. They concern purpose and procedure, so switching models cannot resolve them; this option is unused.

**Sources**: [Anthropic Usage Policy › Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity, High-risk Use Case Requirements, Do Not Use for Surveillance](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup) · [Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy](https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai/use-policy)

questions.title: How Perplexity produces answers
questions.prompt: A Hanbit Trading employee asks Perplexity about recent trends and receives an answer. The employee wants to explain how the service answers questions to a colleague. Which explanation matches the official help documentation?

options.text: It answers only from training data and does not search the internet.
It produces an answer first, then appends source names unrelated to the search results.
It understands the question, searches and summarizes the web in real time, and includes numbered citations linking to original sources.
It searches only within files uploaded by the user.

questions.explanation:
Perplexity’s help documentation describes it as an AI search engine that searches the internet in real time. It understands the question, gathers information from the web, and summarizes it. Each answer includes numbered citations linking to original sources, allowing users to open them and verify the basis for claims.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Perplexity searches the internet in real time to answer questions.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: The citations link to original sources found during the search used to produce the answer; they are not merely appended names.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: Real-time web search and source citations are the answering method described in the help documentation.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, missing condition)**: It is not restricted to uploaded files and can search the wider web.

**Sources**: [What is Perplexity?](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352155-what-is-perplexity) · [How does Perplexity work?](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work)

questions.title: Choosing a Perplexity mode for extensive research
questions.prompt: Nuri Logistics’ planning team needs a draft market report on candidate regions for a new logistics hub. It wants the service to repeatedly search and read documents autonomously from one question, then synthesize many sources into a report. Which Perplexity approach is appropriate?

options.text: Select Deep Research.
Repeatedly use only the basic search that quickly provides a short answer to one question.
Change only the answering model and submit the same question again.
Remove all citation links from the answer and ask again.

questions.explanation:
Perplexity offers search approaches including regular Search, Pro Search, and Deep Research. Its help documentation says Deep Research automatically performs dozens of searches, reads hundreds of sources, and produces a comprehensive report in minutes. This matches delegating repeated searching and a synthesized report from a single question.

- **{{option:A}} (Correct)**: Deep Research produces reports through repeated searching and source synthesis.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, condition mismatch)**: Basic search is intended for quick, short answers rather than delegating repeated searches and report synthesis.
- **{{option:C}} (Incorrect, confusing similar features)**: Model selection determines which model answers; it does not switch the search approach to research-report generation.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, factual error)**: Citation links support verification. Removing them does not broaden the research.

**Sources**: [What is Perplexity?](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352155-what-is-perplexity) · [How does Perplexity work?](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352895-how-does-perplexity-work) · [Introducing Perplexity Deep Research](https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/introducing-perplexity-deep-research)

questions.title: What is available on Hugging Face Hub
questions.prompt: A new member of Hanbit Trading’s data team reads the Hugging Face Hub documentation. Which three components does the documentation introduce as the Hub’s main offerings?

Models, datasets, and Spaces.
Models, internal messaging, and cloud email.
Datasets, Spaces, and coding agents.

- **{{option:B}} (Correct)**: Models, datasets, and Spaces are the components introduced in the documentation.

questions.title: Checking limitations and bias before selecting an open-source model
questions.prompt: Nuri Logistics’ data team is choosing a model on Hugging Face Hub to classify customer inquiries. Where should it look for information about the model’s limitations and biases before adoption?

options.text: Judge it after trying just one demo screen built in Spaces.
Read the description page of another dataset unrelated to the model.
Read the Model Card in that model’s repository.
Compare the number of files uploaded to the model repository.

questions.explanation:
Hugging Face Hub documentation explains that model repositories provide Model Cards to support responsible model use and development by describing limitations and biases. They may also contain information on tasks, languages, and evaluation results. Read the Model Card before adoption to judge suitability for the intended use.

- **{{option:A}} (Incorrect, insufficient evidence)**: Spaces are applications demonstrating models. Trying one demo cannot replace reading information about limitations and biases.
- **{{option:B}} (Incorrect, wrong target)**: An unrelated dataset’s description does not describe the selected model’s limitations.
- **{{option:C}} (Correct)**: The Model Card documents the model’s limitations and biases.
- **{{option:D}} (Incorrect, irrelevant information)**: File counts are unrelated to the model’s limitations and biases.

**Sources**: [Hugging Face Hub documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/index)

questions.title: Checking Firefly before creating advertising concepts
questions.prompt: Hanbit Trading’s advertising team reviews Adobe’s guidance on training data and commercial use before creating product advertising concepts with Adobe Firefly. Select **TWO** statements consistent with the official FAQ.

options.text: Current models were trained on images users collected arbitrarily from the web.
